title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the stratification of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification \hat M_{g,ν} (\bar M_{g,n}) by 'MD-graphs' (Mumford–Deligne graphs), i.e. stable dual graphs with genus weights g_α on vertices and marked legs.

(1) Specialization order. On the previous page he defines [G'] to be a specialization of [G] when \bar M_{G'} ⊂ \bar M_G inside \hat M_{g,ν}. Here he notes that this is a partial order on isomorphism classes of MD-graphs of numerical type (g,ν). It has a greatest element, the trivial graph: one vertex of genus g, ν legs, no edges, whose stratum is the open part M_{g,ν}. He announces that he will refine this order by relating it to morphisms of MD-graphs ('générisations'), which correspond to edge contractions in modern language.

(2) Product decomposition. Each stratum M_[G] admits a finite (étale) covering M_G. In modern terms this is the gluing map ∏_α M_{g_α, \hat I_α} → \bar M_{g,ν}, whose image is the stratum and which is a quotient by Aut(G). Here \hat I_α is the set of marked points at vertex α together with the half-edges at α, and \hat ν_α = ν_α + μ̃_α is its cardinality. Each factor has relative dimension 3(g_α−1)+\hat ν_α over Z.

(3) Dimension count. Summing over the vertices, and using Σ ν_α = ν and Σ μ̃_α = 2 s_1 (each edge has two half-edges), gives
dim M_G/Z = 3Σg_α − 3s_0 + ν + 2s_1.
The next page then uses the genus formula g = Σg_α + h_1 and the Euler characteristic s_0 − s_1 = 1 − h_1 to obtain
dim = 3(g−1) + ν − s_1, i.e. codim M_[G] = s_1 = number of nodes.

All of this is the standard boundary stratification of \bar M_{g,n} (Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen 1983), written in Grothendieck's own language.
errors: The sums Σν_α and Σμ̃_α are written with index α∈S_1 in the image/transcription, but they should run over all vertices α∈S. If S_1 denotes edges, this is a slip of notation; the final result ν + 2s_1 is correct.
'Plus grand élément' is correct only with the convention that specialization means closure containment, so the generic (trivial) graph is the maximum. This is consistent with his definition.

ideas.what: Partial order on stable graph types given by closure inclusion of strata, with the trivial graph as greatest element
ideas.modern_name: Specialization poset of the boundary stratification of \bar M_{g,n}; dual of the edge-contraction order on stable graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); formalized in the language of stable graphs by Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998) and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'tour de Teichmüller' and the stratification at infinity informally

ideas.what: Each stratum is covered by a finite covering which is a product of smaller moduli spaces M_{g_α, n_α}
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / clutching morphisms ξ_G: ∏ \bar M_{g_v,n_v} → \bar M_{g,n}, with image the stratum, quotient by Aut(G)

ideas.what: Dimension formula dim = 3(g−1)+ν−s_1; codimension of a stratum equals the number of edges (nodes)
ideas.modern_name: Codimension of boundary strata = number of nodes

ideas.what: Announced refinement: morphisms ('générisations') of MD-graphs underlying the specialization order
ideas.modern_name: Category of stable graphs with contraction morphisms (modular operads, Getzler–Kapranov; graph categories of Costello, Behrend–Manin)

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans a category of MD-graphs whose morphisms ('générisations') encode the specialization of strata. This anticipates the category of stable graphs with contraction morphisms later central to modular operads. The page itself only announces it, so whether it is genuinely uncredited depends on later pages.
missed.quote: en la reliant à une notion de morphismes (de "générisations") de MD-graphes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an early, independent conception of the stable graph category; it is of historical interest only unless later pages contain more.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard boundary stratification and dimension count of \bar M_{g,n}. The only notable point is the announced category of graph 'générisations', which prefigures later modular-operad formalism but is not developed on this page.
transcription_corrections: The word written above the crossed-out 'est isomorphe' looks more like 'admet' than 'est également', giving: 'chaque M_[G] admet un revêtement fini M_G'.
The marginal annotations under the last line likely read 'poids marqué' (under ν) and 'ordre' (under 2s_1), i.e. ν is the marked weight and 2s_1 the total order/number of half-edges.
The final sums should probably be read as over α∈S (vertices), not α∈S_1.
